Every email that comes in has action items tied to it. So if we had the ability to add a Note/task to that email, it would help us focus on the actionable items of importance. If we open 100 emails a day, that’s a lot of action items. And if we wanted to prioritize those actions of importance, we need an organized way to see those actions. So the tasks would appear in 2 locations exactly the same. Duplicate. One on the task bar as it is today, and the other would appear as a icon of some sort on the email itself. Could you add an icon on the email options for “tasks/notes” with time and date stamps on them so we can get even more strategic on what we are completing first.

title: Looking for a way out
body:
We manage our grocery list collaboratively. I used wunderline to repopulate the list when I reorganized it. I also keep cooking notes and recipes in ToDo. And have another ~90 lists that were imported from Wunderlist. 

ToDo doesn’t have import except from Wunderlist, but the wunderline server is dead. 
ToDo doesn’t have search/replace.
ToDo doesn’t have a print dialogue/capability. 
Search is a nightmare, as it searches all lists. We are out of salt. I need to star “salt” on the grocery list. Searching for salt gets me pages and pages of recipes that include salt. It’s easier to scroll through a 700-item grocery list than search for a simple string. 

I feel betrayed. 

I managed to export a JSON file and will hack that or use it as a template if I can figure out how to reimport the manipulated content. 

Save yourself a major headache and look elsewhere for task management apps.

title: Features are fine but so laggy I frequently give up
body:
UPDATE: Since my original review on June 18, things have gotten worse with the performance on the iPad mini. Now the app hangs and then shuts down before it ever opens on my iPad mini 4. It works “OK” on my iPhone. On a positive note I really like the concept behind the My Day list. I like that it forces you to reassess the things that need to be done each day instead of dragging along all the things that didn’t get accomplished the day before. It would be nice if the planned/scheduled items for each day auto-populated but I can live without that. Also, I t would be nice if the app could be synced with or at least shared with Google calendar. As far as I can tell there is no direct way to do that.

A couple of months ago I dutifully migrated my data from Wunderlist, which I lived by, to To Do. I was prepared to be disappointed, but hopeful that there had truly been integration between the two apps. So far I have found the UI with To Do to be easy to use and I’m navigating subtle changes to organize my days and lists. In this arena I’m pretty happy and there are some things that work even better than Wunderlist. 
Where I am NOT happy is the performance of the app on iOS. I use my iPad Mini 4 for most everything, and almost without fail I am stopped in my tracks by lag every time I use To Do. Half the time I end up abandoning whatever list I’m trying to create because I get so frustrated. If I restart the app it takes forever to reload. My iOS gets updated regularly so I don’t think that’s an issue. I’m more concerned that it’s a Microsoft/Apple compatibility issue, and if so, that would be very disheartening. I never had problems with Wunderlist doing this until Microsoft took it over, but once that happened Wunderlist was laggy too. I really hope this can get worked out. I’d like to be able to continue using To Do
The other issue I have is that I am not allowed to share my personal To Do lists with coworkers on their work Outlook. I had my personal Microsoft account before we had Outlook accounts for work and all my To Do lists are on my personal account. If I can’t share with others from my personal account is there any easy way for me to migrate my personal to do lists to my work Outlook account without copying them all over? Thank you.

title: Wunderlist was Superior
body:
I really cannot stand this app, but I use it because they hijacked Wunderlist and then tossed it in the trash, forcing us into this mess. Yes, it looks very similar to Wunderlist, and they gave a half-*** attempt and making it work like Wunderlist, but it fails in so many areas. 

I feel it’s temperamental. For example, when I’m trying to move an item, it’s is to difficult make sure it goes in between other list items. It’s instead VERY easy to accidentally drop a list item onto another item, forcing that item to become a sub-item under another item, which appears that said action cannot be undone 😳! So we have to delete the sub-item and manually add it back onto the list by creating it a new list item again. This is a huge problem when it comes to my time and productivity. 

The other pretty annoying issue is my completed items populate in my not-completed item list. This may be fine for some tasks, but most certainly is not for a perpetual grocery list. There should be an option on how we’d like to view the completed items. I loved how Wunderlist kept completed tasks at the very bottom so when I needed to view them, I could scroll through ONLY completed items. Now I have to wait for THOUSANDS of completed grocery items that have been purchased over the years to populate (because I imported my Wunderlist). Another huge bog-down in terms of my time and productivity. 

There’s a few other annoyances but
These are the ones that I need fixed to ever be content with Microsoft’s version of Wunderlist.

title: FINALLY Matches & Surpasses Wunderlist!
body: This morning, the creators of “Microsoft To Do” FINALLY fixed enough of the features on this app to meet my former expectations of “Wunderlist!” “Microsoft To Do” (at first) had a lot of fun new features like colorful backgrounds for lists, and a few more sorting options, but was still missing some of the BASICS I enjoyed in “Wunderlist:” Here are my favorite two: 1) Being able to quickly recover a RECENTLY checked-off item at the TOP of the completed items, within a given list. Example: In “To Do” completed items were initially only alphabetized. I have an ongoing (reusable) grocery list including HUNDREDS of products. I even number them, by aisle, to ensure I see them “in order.” (Even if I’m in a different store, it still, at least, “categorizes” them together). But an “accidentally checked off” item, while shopping, was virtually GONE (until I got home & realized what was missing). This was fixed! Now I can just look at the TOP of the completed list. And, 2) Now I can see upcoming tasks separated out BY DAYS. In the past, anything beyond tomorrow was lumped together. Now, just like in Wunderlist, I can quickly find an upcoming day to which a task can be quickly moved/reassigned. And one of my favorite NEWER features of “To Do:” if you want certain tasks to recur/repeat in the future, say, only Mondays Wednesdays & Fridays (as opposed to once a week, or once a day) it can do this! Very cool. Keep up the great work!

Meaning lists I follow to close up the cabin in the fall and other lists to open it in the spring. There is no limit to the type or purpose of lists you can create to make your life easier. 

The big benefit is the ability to check mark ✅ an item to add to a list and check mark ✅ it when it’s finished. This means a list only needs to be typed in one time.

title: Best To-Do minder for today's tasks
body:
Easy to use, with all of the features you need to get today's tasks in front of you.

I use multiple to-do apps. Some are great for complex projects (although MS To-Do allows for multiple steps), some are better for sharing, like grocery lists. But none are as good as MS To-Do for daily, decide the day's priorities and work that list. 

You can add tasks easily to a general pile or a group or directly to My Day. Then drag-and-drop tasks into My Day. Work the list, check off completed items, and My Day is cleared each day forcing you to reconsider what you will work on the next day. 

Within a Group easily move tasks up and down to reflect your priorities. And I use the Stars on a task to give me an easy reminder as to which tasks I want to move back to My Day if I didn't complete the day before. But you can also use the Lightbulb on My Day to bring up yesterday's uncompleted tasks and recently added tasks.

title: NOT designed around the user anymore
body:
Microsoft take over of Wunderlist feels binary. 
It seems to be designed under the assumption that once a task is complete, it is complete for eternity. This strikes me as a male – engineer mindset.
This ignores the probable scenario and common use case of reusable lists.
For example, workouts, grocery shopping, house cleaning, gardening, inventory management, homeschooling, weekly work routines, etc. These activities can involve long “completed“ lists. If you can’t sort those completed lists, they become unwieldy. Basically, they become useless. 

I used to be able to go through my completed lists and turn them back into active to do‘s. Now it’s just too much trouble. If I want to alphabetize a completed list, I have to take 20 minutes to uncheck every item on the completed list to add it back to the uncompleted list, and then run an alphabetize function, and then remember everything that was already done and headed back to the completed list, in reverse alphabetical order.It’s an absurd process you are forcing users to follow in order to make a list reusable. body: I’ll give this app 2-stars because it doesn’t crash ... but seriously, why would anyone WANT to quit using the superior Wunderlist for this half-effort?  Any item you create is stored in the iPhone Reminders as a to-do, but neither scheduled nor shared with associates. Items are not entered by default with a due date, and even if you do add a due or reminder date, they’ll disappear from “today” and don’t carry over to tomorrow, so you must manually add any tasks from a single list of ALL tasks. If you mark an item with a star ... well that’s meaningless. And should you open your iPhone Reminders, you’ll find 100’s of stored there, thereby making simple reminders (like “go to bed”) lost amongst the work tasks that didn’t require being spammed through the Reminders app, not to mention now your to-do of “turn in report” has the same unimportant notification appearance, sound, and limited snooze options as “pick up kids from school”. Utterly worthless and a lesson for how to drive away millions of customers so an app exists solely to have O365 but without any of Wunderlist’s functionality. What a waste.

title: It’s lacking a very important feature
body:
I used our beloved Wunderlist up until the end. And that’s because it had all the best features. I can’t tell you how many apps I’ve downloaded to try and replace Wunderlist, but none of them measured up. They’ve all been deleted. I’m keeping To-Do because I’ve got a little glimmer of hope that they’ll add the one feature that’s keeping me from loving it. 

I used Wunderlist for everything: work, personal life. My favorite was having a “permanent” grocery list of all our usual items. I only starred what I wanted, un-starring when the item was picked up, repeat process. It took the stress out of shopping. In Wunderlist, you can click on the “starred” tab and all the items are beautifully categorized, making shopping a breeze. The whole grocery list was broken down in a way that made sense. 

My ONLY gripe with To-Do is that the starred items aren’t categorized! They’re all jumbled, it’s a total mess and it’s nearly impossible for me to shop the way I used to. Now I to use it to check off items I want, and then I have to write everything down on a piece of paper (for shame) so that I can see it all broken down by category. 

PLEASE allow the starred items to be separated out by category like they were so beautifully in Wunderlist!

title: How Can You Work for 3+ Years to Create A Far Worse App?
body:
See all of the comments here of users bemoaning the loss of Wunderlist.  The developers then respond “please let us know which features you miss.”  It has been years since the purchase of Wunderlist, you would think that they would have taken Wunderlist’s great aesthetic and feature set and advanced them forward. You would unfortunately be wrong.

(This is from Microsoft, the company that normally crams additional features into their software and is concerned that no feature ever gets dropped. )

Anyway, features I miss:
— No quick entry panel on the Mac. See Wunderlist, Todoist, Things, OmniFocus.
—No actual linkage between iOS or Mac Outlook and Todo. See See Wunderlist, Todoist, Things, OmniFocus.
—No linkage to Mac Mail.
—No calendar linkage or support. See Todoist, Things, OmniFocus.
—Nice background colors. Beyond the photo of Berlin, Wunderlist’s backgrounds were nicer. Why can’t we insert our own? Why are there so few?
—No support for Siri Shortcuts. See Wunderlist, Todoist, Things, OmniFocus. What exactly have you been “developing”?
— No Apple Watch app. Microsoft doesn’t have enough developers????  There are companies with One developer that have managed this. 

Overall, I have been a real fan of Microsoft’s development since Satya took over the helm.  But, given the huge head start from the Wunderlist base, and the developer capability of Microsoft, it’s hard to imagine how they could have done this more poorly.  This is a very competitive space—if Todo were really “Wunderlist on Steroids” they wouldn’t be forcing Wunderlist customers off the platform, they would have jumped already with no coaxing.

title: Don’t normally write reviews.
body:
Anybody migrating from Wunderlist will not be happy with this app as it currently stands. It will require updates to include features you previously used and relied on. Until those features are included, you might need to look elsewhere.

Wunderlist was a fantastic app with incredibly intuitive features that greatly improved efficiency. When you have a great app, why change it? Overall this is a shell of the Wunderlist app and is missing the key features that made the app so powerful and user friendly.

Missing calendar feed: this was probably my favorite feature as it allowed me to see my upcoming tasks in my iCalendar.

Missing smart scheduling feature: in Wunderlist you could type in the task line: “Submit paper April 31 11:59pm” and it would automatically insert the due date and time. Less things to click and scroll through aka more efficient. Migrating from Wunderlist, I expected at the very least a poorly designed smart scheduling feature.

Additionally, My Day should automatically transfer over things that are due today. That would seem pretty logical to me. It makes me feel like there’s some disconnect and I become uneasy about possibly forgetting something which is the opposite of the feeling I should be getting while using this app.

If I wasn’t somebody who had used Wunderlist daily for 5 years, my review might be more favorable. This app has incredible potential to become #1 on the App Store productivity category, but the developers are going to need to listen to the team that developed Wunderlist and it’s migrating users.

My only complaints are that the UI could use some small adjustments. I like to check off items, but then after, I have to delete them. I'm hoping these things will get fixed over time but so far I'm enjoying the app!

title: Buggy still
body:
A great start and I’m happy so far. I used to be an avid user of Astrid and Wunderlist, and have been pretty frustrated these good apps keep getting bought by mega corporations. (Yahoo and Microsoft)

For this app, there are some bugs and quirky behaviors that are frustrating. I migrated from Wunderlist and these weren’t issues before. Some example below:

- The weekly recurring tasks don’t work. Just try it. If I set it for Friday, it somehow labels it as “Thu, Fri”. Is it a time zone issue? I’m in ET.
- The sorting doesn’t work well. As we could in Wunderlist or even Excel, a sort order should not lock the list. We should still be able to move items around. Imagine a use case, where I want the list to be first sorted by items in the order they were created...then I want to reorder some items to appear on top.  Not possible right now. We just end up having a jumbled mess. 
- When you inadvertently check off an item, it’s almost impossible to find it to uncheck it if you had Completed Items hidden. In Wunderlist, when a task is completed, it gets sent to the bottom and they are sorted in the order which they were completed. Now not anymore. It’s jumbled elsewhere and due to the weird sorting behavior (mentioned above), I can’t find it. 
- No easy way to purge completed items? This should be a setting. I had hundreds maybe thousands in some lists, and I had to manually delete each one. (I had to because I felt the app was slow.)

It also seems like a lot of effort has been put in to keeping existing features of the different sources available, which is important because each source has its strengths.

title: Bleh
body:
I was a Wunderlist user and I used it for very simple things - groceries, personal to-do’s, etc. Light, simple use. Loved Wunderlist. I’ve experienced Issues with this app that seem very basic to me, though. For example:
- Synching is buggy. I share several lists with my wife and somehow we end up with lists that aren’t exactly the same sometimes. Just got home from the grocery store, wife’s list has hamburger buns, mine didn’t. Watched as we synched again and still not on my list. Of course additional trips to the grocery store are now not so routine.
- when I toggle the app to show items crossed off a list, that works. When I toggle back to not showing them it freezes. Every. Single. Time.
- it won’t let me move something to the very bottom of the list. Have to move it to second to last, then move the last item up one.
- seems very easy to inadvertently cross something off when scrolling compared to Wunderlist.
- the nesting feature seems nice in concept, but it’s very easy to accidentally nest something under another to-do item when moving things around on an iPhone, and for the life of me I can’t figure out how to un-nest it. So, stuck with deleting it and adding it again.

I would expect some bugs from a fairly new app but seems like Microsoft should be able to do better than the average little app builder. So, we’re gonna use Wunderlist until we can’t then find something else.

So now the app puts no tasks at the top of the list instead of the bottom, just like Wunderlist (RIP). I’ve changed my review to 5 star accordingly. This is a GREAT To Do list app. Well done! 

Original Review:
Ok, I say that tongue-and-cheek... but I really do like this app, and I think that it replaces Wunderlist, which I’ve used since it first came out, very well. Except for one thing. Please, PLEASE, give us the option to add new tasks to the top of the list instead of the bottom. Just a simple toggle will do. title: Can be frustrating to use
body:
I used Wunderlist to keep running meal plans and a grocery list. I switched over to To Do when they emailed us about phasing out the app. Since using to do, I have been annoyed with the “show completed tasks” feature. It’s easy to accidentally check off an item that you haven’t completed. In Wunderlist, I could quickly figure out what I clicked by accident, because it kept the crossed off item in the same location in the list (showed it in it’s original location with the uncompleted tasks still there). In to do, if you say to show completed tasks, it pulls them up in a totally different order... like a running list of completed to do’s. There is no way for me to figure out which one I just removed from my list by mistake. 

My app is also freezing up when I say “hide completed tasks”. It won’t go back to my list. I have to shut the app down and reopen it. 

When scrolling sometimes the app thinks I’ve selected a task and moves it... I understand the desire to rearrange items, but I would rather that be a separate menu or something. I make my grocery list in an order to begin with. I don’t want that order changed because I’m scrolling. Maybe include an edit option that allows you to move items, but make items stay put unless you specifically tap the dot to check them off. 

Too much happens by accident!

title: Wunderlist Pros/Cons
body:
PROS:

— Microsoft uses Wunderlist’s simple user interface. Great!

— Importing non-shared lists from Wunderlist was straightforward although a bit slow.

CONS:

— Recreating shared lists from Wunderlist is dreadful. This is because each person must install the ToDo app and import all of his or her private lists for their devices and accounts. But the import process creates a private list on each person’s devices for each shared list. Getting back to a single shared list requires everyone to delete the imported private list having the name of the shared list to allow the owner to re-share his or her original imported list.  This was tedious with just two-person sharing. I can’t imagine the difficulty in setting up your devices if lists are shared with multiple persons having different owners.

— By default, lists are imported with completed tasks showing. Hiding a long list of completed task takes forever, and locks up the app while it is being done.

— There is no way to determine if a shared list is in sync with other users. You have to dig to find the mechanism to manually sync a list. Even after doing a manually sync, my shared grocery list does not contain the latest item that my spouse added to the list. (I’ve been waiting 30 minutes.) I can’t imagine using MicroSoft ToDo for a joint shopping trip to the grocery store. This is something my spouse and I did often with Wunderlist to split up the shopping effort while both of us were in the same store. I’ve contacted support in this regard, and will update this review with a response (if I receive one.)

I will update this review as I find other issues. Good luck!

title: Transitioning is a little painful
body:
I’m transitioning off Wunderlist and am giving MS to do a try. The import was very quick and easy so I appreciate that. The app itself is similar although there are some key issues that are causing very big annoyances with daily use. 

Overall, this is a great app that is FREE. We’re so used to getting all these from Wunderlist that sometimes we don’t take the time to appreciate the work that is done and offered for free.  Thank you. 

The items below are a few area where the app can be improved. 

Accidental actions. I’ve noticed that I’ve been accidentally marking things a lot while trying to scroll. I started comparing the two apps and noticed that Wunderlist was superb at this.  

In Wunderlist the whole horizontal space was scrollable, include the checkbox and the star. This made scrolling extremely easy and prevented any accidental marking tasks. Only when you really narrowed in and wanted to mark something, did it actually mark the task. 

In To Do, The vertical scrolling is limited to the text in the middle and not to the checkbox or the star on the edges. Because of this, when you try to scroll near the left or right edge, you end up accidentally marking something completed or important. This seems to be happening a lot.. at least for me (could be user error)... the actions seem a little too sensitive. 

When you accidentally mark something complete, there is no undo and therefore you must go to show “completed items”, search for it and uncheck the item.  This has become very cumbersome. 

Also, Another review mentioned it, but the “planned” section (previously) “Week” has become rather clutter. I see the idea they are going for, however, this section works better as a high level view of your week instead cluttering it with too much information, grouped in an impractical way.  When you get to Saturday or Sunday, the next week is clumped into one section and that is not helpful. 

The idea is nice but I don’t see if being as useful as a simple week view separated by days. It would be great to at least show the next 5 days (or however many) split out. 

Thank you and keep up the great work.

title: A Lesser Wunderlist
body:
The app has potential, but the “My Day” feature should not be a forced feature.  

I prefer the “Today” menu in Wunderlist, which was sectioned by project and was easy to control.  It was so simple that Wunderlist became my note taking tool anytime I need to quickly jot something down.  I didn’t have to worry about the note getting lost deep in the tasks, since it appeared as one of the today’s tasks.  From there, once again, it was easy to control.

The “My Day” feature poses as a decluttering tool, but is really a redundancy that forces there to be two due dates to a task instead of one.  “Today” was same as “My Day”, except you mark whatever you will not be able to do today vs. marking what you will be able to do today.  At the very least, we should have both options.

This app beats Wunderlist in the sync feature, notes functionality, app crashes, and design.  But, the fundamentals are lackluster for a Microsoft product.  Users being forced off Wunderlist to this is unfortunate.

Now, since we are forced to move away from Wunderlist to the lessor Microsoft To Do app, I will have to spend time finding and migrating again over to another better app that allows me a simple option to directly print my lists from my iPhone via AirPrint straight to my networked home printer.

title: Not Terrible but There’s Issues
body:
So I’m trying to wean myself off Wunderlist to the To Do app and while it’s not terrible there are issues. For one I’m not crazy about the Planned section at all. If anything it feels cluttered and unorganized. The earlier tab brings up tasks I’ve not set dates for and ironically haven’t used recently but the only way I can remove them is by marking them as complete and 100% eliminating them. So unless I want to continuously create a new  shopping task rather than edit the preexisting one in my earlier tab I guess they’ll have to hang around uselessly in Planned. The other issue I have with Planned is how jumbled up the rest of the week looks when you’re trying to see what tasks are coming up. In Wunderlist your week was sectioned into days and your tasks were allotted to those days. Now the tasks are all piled together under one tab that accounts for most of the week and it just seems like unnecessary clutter. 
The other issues I came across was that “My Day” doesn’t auto populate which seems rather redundant and I preferred when the important tasks moved to the top of the lists. It would also be really awesome to move the tasks assigned to each day in an order of importance if that became available. 
I know To Do is still an app in progress but I do rely upon my planners a lot and hope it eventually becomes as successful as the beloved Wunderlist.
author: nyx74

title: Still Has a Long Way to Go to Match Wunderlist
body:
As a very longtime daily user of Wunderlist, I recently downloaded MTD and imported my Wunderlist lists. Figured what the hey — Wunderlist is eventually going to be phased out anyway. To my surprise, MTD is missing a lot of the basic functionality that makes Wunderlist useful. 

First and foremost, when you tag a todo item with a star, it does not push that item to the top of the list. Instead you have to sort by the starred items and then manually rearrange them by dragging them around if you want to sort by priorities. This feels regressive — with Wunderlist, it was much more convenient to tap the star icon and sort your priorities that way. This feels incredibly tedious by comparison and it feels more like the application is being developed solely for desktop rather than from a mobile-first perspective. 

Also, the “daily focus” feature on MTD feels entirely useless, as other reviewers here have noted. It’s also way too tedious and unintuitive to be useful. The “starred” list view also is fundamentally flawed — instead of breaking them out into subsections by list category like Wunderlist does, it just inelegantly lumps them all into the same list. This makes that feature essentially unusable when I am using lists to manage different areas of my personal and professional life. How is it useful that my “buy milk” list item is sitting there right below my “complete TPS report” list item with no separation or context about the list they came from? Just show how little attention to detail has been put into harvesting the “best features” of Wunderlist if this one got left on the cutting room floor. 

And finally, I know this is a minor gripe that shouldn’t matter, but I really liked Wunderlist’s overall interface. You could set a background (there’s no readily apparent way to do this in MTD), it had some warm colors in the list items themselves, and the list item menus (subtasks, etc) just had an excellent user experience. I get that some of these elements may have seemed slightly skeuomorphic or frivolous to Microsoft’s dev team. By contrast, though, MTD is clunky, corporate and generally missing many of the little features and usability flourishes that I enjoyed for the past 7+ years of using Wunderlist. 

I’m also not crazy about being forced to login using a Microsoft account and integrated into that ecosystem of software — I would strongly prefer having the option of being able to just login using my existing Wunderlist credentials or a gmail account or something. 

I’m not entirely sure why Microsoft would acquire a popular app like Wunderlist and then proceed to reinvent the wheel with its own essentially inferior application. As a longtime user, I think WL deserves better than being stripped for parts and only “integrating the best features” as the Microsoft development team claims. I’d really been hoping they’d just reskin the existing application and start from that point, but I suppose that would have been too easy for a company that’s well-known for making unintuitive and over-engineered moves like this. 

Anyway, I’m going to delete the app for now and hope that more of Wunderlist’s functionality finds its way into the app before I’m ultimately forced to convert to it. Fingers crossed.

title: What I was looking for
body:
I’m a huge fan of the Outlook to-do list and to-do bar, and this app is the perfect compliment to managing productivity with Outlook. The syncing with Outlook is essential, and it’s the reason I am excited about this app.

When I’m trying to get stuff done, I’m on my phone all the time. I desperately needed a way to get and keep my tasks in front of me, which meant I needed them on my phone to do that. Microsoft To-Do was the obvious solution—I had all my flagged emails and tasks on my Outlook client; I just needed them on my phone too. 

Very happy with the smart lists and the fact that I now have ONE to do list instead of a list scratched down in a notebook, one on the fridge, one on a note-taking app, and then my list of flagged emails. 

I need to also mention the most important feature of all: the PLING you get when you check off a task. The app wouldn’t be the same without it.

title: Just forced from Wunderlist
body:
I just hired a new employee, who Wunderlist blocked from creating a new account. This forced my team to make an immediate move to To-Do, which in its current state is not as good as Wunderlist. 

We have many team members with assignments to be completed in order, but the “Assigned to You” list does not allow you to sort by due date, or any other way. 

The list provides too much detail, with little color variety, which makes it harder to find the information you need (like the due date). Wunderlist displayed this perfectly. 

The UI is clunky as well. I like to keep my list slender on one side of my laptop screen, but if you click into an item it expands the window automatically, and does not revert. 

If you are a part of a shared list your are forced to use the theme of the list owner. You cannot set your own theme in this case. 

I would have been ok with the forced transition if To-Do was an improvement, but it is not. There is a flood of improvement requests on the forum, which is discouraging. I fear my issues will not be fixed any time soon, if at all.

title: Developers Of App PLEASE READ
body:
I love the app, it beats the reminders app in some ways, so use it as my main task manager currently today. 

However, please catch up with Reminders app in these ways. 

1. Let us select pictures from photos and add it to any task, like added info to the text, but optional room n each new task created.

2. The main screen where you can make a folder, or just see the individual task categories you make, give is the ability to change the symbol on the left hand side to hundreds of symbols to choose from. Also let us change the color of the symbols. This helps users visualize where they need to go quicker when opening the app, and more easy to use and manage list of we have lots of categories. 

3. Give us the ability to love around and hide the default list at the top, so app is easier to use. That way it’s like a “desktop” computer, think of it that way. If we don’t use a feature much on windows desktop, we probably don’t want a “shortcut” link to that app that we cannot move or hide always there. So ability to hide default list if can’t delete them. 

4. Also please add a feature, kind of goes with number 3, to let us change the theme of the home screen of the app. This way we can choose how to “visualize” our list on a way that best works for a user, since everyone is different. 

5. Last several times I have list shared to me, and they would get an error. We would try again the next day and normally no problems second time. 

6. Would be cool to be able to add voice memos as well to a specific task. 

Thank you, love the app, just think would be number one app in world in take in these ideas.

title: The most important app on my phone
body:
I picked up this app on my iPhone and Mac, hoping I could work it into my routine at work and solve some of my team’s productivity and communication issues. To Do quickly became the lifeline of my business in exactly the way I had hoped, by organizing all of our messy actions and projects across multiple lists shared among various team members. In addition to typical tools in the toolbox, such as “Reminder,” “Due Date,” “Steps” and others, the addition of “My Day” and “Assign To” are unique to me tools I use every single day.  

To Do is incredibly simple to use and understand. In addition to work, I’ve been using it as well for my personal life, and other professional projects and volunteer work. Doing this has only strengthened my commitment to it, while my past experience with to do apps was almost always short-lived. 

Few other apps, if any, bring a simplified, high level of organization and teamwork to productivity as this one does- at a cost of nothing. 

I’m looking forward to updates with new features and further integration with Outlook and other Microsoft tools, but right now, this is already the best and most important app I use, hands down!

title: It’s like it was made by someone who never uses these things
body:
I’m trying to embrace change, having been a lifetime Wunderlist user, but some of the behavior here is downright bizarre. I don’t feel like this is even a lateral move.

First off, having tasks scheduled for TODAY’S date should force them into the ‘My Day’ list. This seems like default behavior to me. Having to manually search for and add them is counterproductive. 

What happens to tasks I move to ‘My Day’ that aren’t completed and become overdue?  Tomorrow they’re just... gone. Poof! 

The tasks on the ‘planned’ and ‘important’ screens should be grouped by the parent list. It feels incoherent.  Many tasks don’t make sense when they’re orphaned from their parent.

Overall the app seems a bit half-baked, I’m disappointed.

title: Almost as good as Wunderlist
body:
Microsoft has done a good job replacing Wunderlist (which they bought) with To Do, and making it pretty easy to migrate from Wunderlist to To Do. Overall, functionality is everything you’d need to manage your tasks. 

Things to improve: 

1. Make it easier to migrate from Wunderlist WITH people you previously shared lists with. It took my wife and me an hour to figure that out. Not a great way to get started. 

2. Allow users to set default order for new tasks. Currently they always go to the bottom of the list. I’d prefer to have them go to the top, like I could do in Wunderlist. 

3. If you accidentally drop a task onto another task, it will turn it into a sub task. Not a bad feature, except that you can’t drag that sub task back “up” to turn it back into a task.  Or if you can, it’s not at all obvious how to do so. 

4. Moving tasks between lists is cumbersome. You can’t just drag and drop it, like you could on Wunderlist. You have to Edit the list, then move it. Extra clicks, and unintuitive, ugh.

title: Issues w Microsoft App Developers
body:
Update: needs multi account syncing. Have a business account and personal. I can only use one. 

I’ve been thinking about transitioning from Apple iCloud based apps to apps that work on all hardware platforms. What I am finding is that iOS has the market cornered on the quality of Apps in its App Store. 

I’ve also been very turned off by the smaller app developers and their push to subscription based plans and lack. I don’t want a freaking subscription to every app! Plus I find that it’s not really worth it unless the hardware company offers cloud storage, optimized apps and supports them along with its hardware on multiple platforms. 

App developers have handled the move to iOS 13 poorly. They have been slow to update, switching to subscription models on previously owned apps and only My Lord knows if the app will be updated with the features you want. 

With companies like Apple, Google and Microsoft you know what you get. I’m afraid of Google because of it privacy policy, but it has solid apps. Apple is apple. Hardware is good, but apps are basic. Microsoft seems to be showing a lot of promise lately, but I think there app developers are poor. I am coming to believe that they intentionally hold back from full iOS integration. If it’s not intentional, then it’s just plan silliness considering their mission and that they no longer have a phone. 

I’m going to post this on each of the Microsoft apps and hope that it gets someone’s attention. Lol

Microsoft Todo:

Lacks Share Extension support
Can’t email a todo into the app. 
Isn’t integrated with iOS search which is huge while on the go. 
Outlook: 

Took months to get calendar search. Calendar such only works with outlook accounts. (I would move to this app if I could search my calendar)
Printing an attachment isn’t always straight forward. I tried to print a word document and had to convert it to pdf. 
New design is clunky and cluttered. 
Slow splash page at launch. 
Phantom updates and fixes. 
OneNote:

Slow splash page at launch. 
Isn’t integrated with iOS search which is huge while on the go. 
Just sharing my thoughts. I’m just noticing a lack of consistency across third party apps which keeps me with boring old apple services.

title: Needs improvement
body:
I am a long-time Wunderlist user whom finally made the switch. The import took about an hour and went smooth. 

I really wanted to like this app. I was hopeful ToDo would be closer to Wunderlist than it is.  If you don’t have date based items this app would be perfect.  With dates, it’s been a complete struggle (TickTick app will be my next home). 

My top 3 deal breakers:

1- There is no badge notification indicator remaining items left for the day.  Absurd!

2- There is no dedicated “Today” view. It is replaced by “My Day” and then clicking suggestions (another tap).  This ironically includes items with due dates of today, tomorrow and items in the future.  “My Day” doesn’t just display items with a due date of the current date (and overdue items).   I’m guessing because the implementation of “My Day” is so obscure is the very reason there are no badge notifications. 

3- There is no dedicated “week” (7 day) view. It is replaced by “planned” which lists items sorted by today, tomorrow and then everything else. 

Wunderlist excelled at minimalistic simplicity. This app is not there yet.

1) The ability to easily see what Tasks (and Steps) were completed during a specified time frame. This would be useful in meetings when sharing out recently completed items. 
2) The ability to schedule due dates for Steps. This would provide flexibility in the way individuals choose to use the app. For example: my tasks are commonly medium sized project, which would benefit from multiple due dates. I could achieve this functionality by making a new list for each medium sized project, but it seems a bit cumbersome to do so. 

Overall, I am thrilled with the app and its place in the Microsoft ecosystem. Just looking for it to grow a little more.

title: Wunderlist vs To Do
body:
I’d like to echo the sentiments in the review below entitled “Doesn’t hold a candle to Wunderlist.”

In addition to the issue about listing items in “My Day” on the day they are due, I am also disappointed that when you change a due date, the reminder doesn’t automatically update.  
This was a great feature in Wunderlist which I took for granted until forced to try To Do (as Wunderlist will be discontinued by Microsoft). 
When changing the due date of an item in To Do, one has to take the 2 extra steps of re-entering the reminder day and time.  For example, I updated an overdue task for a future date.  Wunderlist would automatically 
update the reminder date/time to 9am of the new due date.  In To  Do, the reminder date/time remains in the past (literally says “Remind me at 10am yesterday”)  and the quick options in the reminder pick list (“later today”, “tomorrow,” “next week”) are not helpful if the new due date is say a month away. One has to: click on reminders, select “pick a date and time”, scroll to the correct month (it defaults to the past month) and finally pick the new reminder date/time.  

I hope MS will address this limitation on To Do

title: Gets Cluttered Fast
body:
This is like every other notepad app out there, meaning it does nothing helpful for how people put together real life task lists. I use my iPhone’s notepad with checkboxes, and manually update tasks for everything i do. Some are daily, some are long-term. So of course a real to do list app would be able to organize that right? And allow daily tasks to reoccur and be completed daily, alongside long-term ones. Well this app, like all the others, doesn’t. 

You can make tasks reoccur... but they won’t show up in ‘My Day’ by default. BUT after you complete one for the day (eg. Brush teeth), it’ll just reappear randomly in the list with subtext of ‘tomorrow’, which is beyond useless, beyond unintuitive or logical, and clutters the entire list. Then the whole ‘My Day’ feature gets pretty dumb if tasks can’t autopopulate there. All in all, giving Microsoft the responsibility to make something intuitive is always bound to fail, so this is really just like every other worthless, weakly supported, temporarily-named, overlapping functionality MS product out there. Win10’s, and to a lesser extent the Office suite is fine (necessary evils really, you can’t escape Windows or Office), but don’t let that fool you into thinking ANYTHING else they ever introduce in their ecosystem is useful or useable.

title: One of my few ‘essential’ apps
body: I almost never write app reviews but wanted to give some praise to this outstanding app. I used to use post-it notes and text documents on my computer to organize all my ‘to do’ lists. But they often became rather large and unwieldy with both work and home tasks combined. I wanted a better way to organize my tasks as well as a way to always have my list on hand for when something new came to mind. An iPhone app was the best solution, and the To Do app has fit the bill perfectly. Within just a few months of use, it has become an essential part of my planning for all of my tasks at both work and home.  Though the interface is simple and straightforward, you come to see the app is quite sophisticated as you explore its capabilities. You can organize to-do items within folders and add ‘Steps’ as sub tasks within the main task item itself. Items can be tagged for addition to the main ‘My Day’ folder, where all your planned tasks for that day reside until you check them off.  Tasks not completed by midnight can be reviewed the following day and added again to the ‘My Day’ folder or allowed to remain in their custom home folder until another day. Tasks can be designated as planned events, with future dates assigned for their completion. You can set both the due date and when you want a notification to remind you about them.  The app has the ability to assign tasks to others using the same app, but I don’t use that function. My only wish for improvement is the creation of a ‘My Weekend’ folder similar to the ‘My Day’ folder. That would help with planning my days off during the course of my work week. I’ve created a work-around by making a custom folder for weekend tasks, but custom folders lack some of the features of the main ‘My Day’ folder.

title: Best To-Do List App I have Found
body:
I would have to say that overall Microsoft To-Do is a fantastic app and definitely the best to-do list app I have used. They make it very easy for someone with an ever growing and changing list of things that need to be done to organize everything in their life. 
For example: I have my main tasks listed in the default list but I also have a list for each of the jobs I work, and a group with lists for all of my college classes and their assignments. And the best part is you can view everything that needs to be done today, tomorrow, next week, and later from all of those lists all on one page in the “Planned” tab. This app also works really well across multiple platforms by instantly syncing changes. I use it on my iPhone, iPad, and Windows PC. 
A main feature I would really love to see added for the versions on iOS and iPadOS is the ability to add Microsoft To-Do to your widgets this way you can see and check things off your list all right from your home screen. 
My biggest complaint is that whenever you add a task from the “Planned” tab it defaults to being due yesterday??? But overall it’s a to-do list app and I think you would have a really difficult time finding a better one out there.

title: It’s a glorified piece of paper
body:
Save your time and download one of the other, much better task management apps out there that are free and have much more functionality that this app. This app is really nothing more than a glorified piece of paper that you scribble your next days tasks on each night. 

Other apps - like TickTick, Todoist or any of the other well known task management apps - offer better tag support, smart lists, much better search functionality and many other features. How Microsoft, one of the largest companies in the world can put out software that is barely more functional than a notepad is beyond me. 

The big update this app got after god knows how long was that we can now change the background color of lists?!?!?!?  Does Microsoft only have high school level interns working on this app?  They could have just rebranded Wunderlist (which they own) and had a more functional app. 

If work didn’t require me to use this app, i would have deleted it a long time ago.

title: Unable to Use in Conjunction with iOS Outlook App
body:

And, what good is that when the To-Do’s application lacks the same functionality on iOS mobile? The valuable ways Outlook Tasks (the desktop name for To-Do’s) can be used in concert with Outlook’s calendar and e-mail are impossible to reproduce using this stand-alone To-Do’s app.

This means for those of us who use Outlook calendar, e-mail and tasks together, those of us who are getting more benefit from Outlook because we’re using more of its power, must return to our desktop in order to finish our work. We cannot do it all in a single application.

There is a third-party e-mail app which allows the user to create tasks, as well as create tasks from e-mails. Why does Microsoft choose to keep these features out of their own iOS version of their iOS Outlook program?

title: Off to a great start, but needs maturing.
body:
Pros: 
- User friendly for what it offers
- Fluid, simple interface. Isn’t confusing to know what you’re doing.
- Easy to prioritize tasks
- Each task can be broken up into items (very useful for projects and/purchasing)

Cons
- Minimal navigation ability on completed tasks. Only way to navigate completed tasks is by opening up a list where it’s all dumped into. It may be in chronological order, but it’s difficult to know for sure. This leads me to my second issue...
- Completed tasks don’t have a date of completion listed next to it unless you click on the individual task. So if you want to know what you completed in a particular week a couple months ago, you have to keep clicking on items until you find the date of interest. title: This is my favorite to-do app
body:
Note: I use todo apps for myself and cannot comment on sharing capabilities or lack thereof.

I have tried several todo apps and this one is my favorite.  I have been using it for more than a year.

I appreciate the simplicity of this app.  It is easy to use.  And it has a clean look I prefer.  I also like the color scheme.  And I really like the My Day list.  I like that we start fresh each day.  I also like that if we don’t get to all those items today then the next day it will appear as a suggestion to add to My Day.  

I thought that we couldn’t move items from one list to another, but I just discovered we can!  I don’t know if that was included in one of the updates or if the feature has always been there and I just didn’t realize.

A recent update allows users to star priority items, which is a nice feature.

Oh and I do also appreciate that there is a desktop version of this app that syncs with the phone version.  I haven’t used the desktop version in awhile , but I appreciate that it’s there.

A minor complaint - I would like to be able to do multiple sorts on a list.  For the My Day list, I want to arrange the items in order of which task I am going to do first.  But I also want to sort by completed tasks so completed tasks are moved to the bottom.  I know I can just hide completed tasks, but for My Day I like to be able to see what I accomplished.

Actually, I think completed tasks should automatically be moved to the bottom without having to sort them.

8/05/18 in an update, when we pull up the app it takes us to the last list we worked on instead of My Day.  I liked it better before.  I mostly use My Day and when I go to a different list it is just for the moment so I usually don’t need to work on that list when I pull up the app again.

10/17/18 I don’t like the way repeating tasks are handled.   If we don’t complete the task by the due date,  when we complete the task it shows next date due from the last date due instead of the date we actually completed it.  So if, for example, I have a task that repeats weekly, and I am overdue by two weeks, but I complete it today, then the next due date will show as last week.  It doesn’t take into account that I only completed the task today so now the next due date should be a week from today.

title: Doesn’t hold a candle to Wunderlist
body:
I have been a happy user of Wunderlist for the last couple of years. It’s an exceptional app for organizing your to do list. There was another reviewer that hit the nail on the head with this. The biggest flaw with this To-Do app is that you cannot organize and categorize your tasks in a given day. Why have smart list if your app won’t organize them by smart list? It doesn’t make sense. 

In the Wunderlist app you enter tasks, you categorize them and then for any given day all the things that you need to do for the day are grouped in the different categories. it’s a simple concept and shouldn’t be too difficult to enable. 

For example if you go to the grocery store, you don’t go in with a list that has everything all mixed up on one long list. In order to be efficient, you typically will group things by area in the store. You’ll put all of your vegetables together all of your dairy etc. That way you’re not running around the store in a disorganized fashion and missing things on your list.

 Same thing with managing your daily tasks. It takes way too many brain cells to try to jumble everything up. They need to be categorized so that your brain doesn’t have to do too much work. 

Very disappointed in this app and I hope Wunderlist stays around in the ether for a while so I can continue to use it. Will have to find something else because To-Do does not cut it.

title: Please give up and just keep Wunderlist
body:
There have been more than enough users who have said this. It's not that To-do is that terrible in of itself, but Wunderlist compared to To-do is like a Tesla Models S compared with a somewhat good-looking bicycle. Wunderlist even integrates better with other Microsoft products than To-do! 

I know Wunderlist was purchased by Microsoft several years ago, but take a page from what Microsoft did when they bought Acompli and Sunrise and rebranded them into a very successful Outlook for iOS. Or when Microsoft bought LinkedIn and Github and made plans to invest in and improve them over time, rather than rip and replace them. 

The list of features and functionality that Wunderlist has that To-do doesn't have (and probably won't have) is far too long for this review, and I bet the product managers for To-do already know this as they struggle to prioritize new features for To-do. Don't bother! Don't be stubborn, arrogant, or whatever is holding you back! Copy the code if you have to! Be smart: just rebrand Wunderlist and look like a genius!

title: Improving, update by update
body:
To-Do has definitely improved from my first download a year ago, but there are still key features that keep me with Wunderlist (app/company was acquired by Microsoft and that team now works on To-Do). 

Pros of To-Do that have me looking forward to a move from Wunderlist:
- Dropped the skeuomorphic design
- Has Wunderlist import feature (some reviews say this is still a little buggy)
- The font is clean and visually pleasing 

Features Wunderlist has that To-Do still needs:
- Folders and nesting for lists: I prefer to break out different projects and responsibilities within my work list
- Option for a scrolling calendar wheel, or the ability to have weeks start on Monday, not Sunday when setting task due dates. I’m fine with the “Pick a date” calendar option, but I would SO prefer the ability to have this calendar have Mondays to start weeks. I’ve been able to do this in Outlook, so I know you can add this feature 😊
- Ability to update profile photo: Currently cannot update the standard avatar
- Variety of neutral backgrounds: With To-Do, the background of the “Important” list cannot be altered. For now it’s an uneditable purple space telescope theme. I tried to swap every list to be a plain neutral blue with no cartoon drawings. Some people may love the cartoons, but I need more neutral color options and just want to focus on my to dos, especially the ones I’ve noted are most important!

title: Some suggestions from a Wunderlist user
body:
1. Have pre-defined filtered views: Starred/flagged, Today, Week, overdue. The “My Day” function serves as a manual populated list which creates more work. Having the pre-defined filters will allow us to quickly glance at what we need to do. Remember, to-dos are for quick activities not fussing around with manually populating. Maybe rename the My Day to “flagged/starred” items. Week view should at least show the next 3-4 days.

2. Ability to “star/flag” items without having to open the task. In Wunderlist a star was next to the item. Why not create the same but with the “My Day” icon?

3. Add priorities (H/M/L/1/2/3...)

4. When setting up the Due Date for a task, selecting Next Week pushes to Sunday as opposed to one week from the original date. This should be an easy fix.

5. When adding a “Next Step”, have the cursor ready for another entry. For example, when I enter multiple “Steps”, I have to keep touching the “+ Next Step” for each entry. Just like the existing function of adding multiple To-Dos.

Keep up the good work!

title: Why...?
body:
If you sold cheese, you wouldn't introduce a super boring cheese with less flavor and then tell everyone that eventually it would be as good as the cheese you were discontinuing. 

Why not make Microsoft To-Do (at least) as good as Wunderlist (functionally), first, and then release it? I don't understand? Then, and only then, officially announce the demise of Wunderlist. 

Things that are brilliant about Wunderlist:

- Simplicity of user experience without being over simplified. 

- Visual space and UI  is smartly organized. Edit actions in Wunderlist are within easy reach of where your thumbs already are at the bottom of the screen, not just at the top right.

- Collaboration (a key feature)

- Simple, intuitive, collapsing and expanding folder organization (a key feature)

- Force touch edit capability and/or a drag and drop to move/edit a list items. To-Do pales in comparison to Wunderlist at moving and editing list items with extra steps to get a simple job done.

I want a simple list app that delights and gets out of my way. Microsoft To-Do is not that.

title: Needs a lot of work
body: I am a physician and a scientist who requires a good to-do app to keep everything straight on a daily basis. Wunderlist was really the perfect tool for this, allowing me to organize and share tasks with lab members and clinical colleagues. When I learned it would eventually replace wunderlist, I decided to give To-Do a solid try. I imported all my lists from wunderlist, familiarized myself with all of To-Do’s features, and used it in place of Wunderlist for a good week. Unfortunately, a year after it’s unveiling, To-Do still needs a lot of work. The lack of a way to group related lists and the inability to automatically place tasks that are due today into the “my day” folder are critical deficiencies. Sure you can click the lightbulb in the “my day” folder and select all the upcoming tasks with the help of “suggestions,” but many (like me) cant remember to do that on a daily basis. The point of a to-do app is to make remembering all of your daily tasks unnecessary. I had so many issues with missing things (I literally have a hundred tasks some days) that I had to switch back to Wunderlist within a week. I know that the Microsoft team is working hard on To-Do behind the scenes. I plan to keep checking in and switch to to-do once it truly integrates all the features of wunderlist.

title: Half-Baked
body: This app and its web counterpart need a lot more work. It would be great if they combined it with Outlook Tasks and Planner into a single task management system, akin to Todoist. The app needs natural language support, a desktop Mac client, tie-ins with Teams to create tasks and projects directly from Teams, and tasks dated for today need to be automatically added to My Day so everything due in a given day is all in one place, rather than looking from list to list. It would also be great if it had a general Inbox to add tasks to as they come to mind and then organize later, like GTD prescribes. List sharing would be another big boost, especially for businesses if it’s linked to Teams, so that projects could be organized through ToDo and tasks managed. Apps like TickTick or Todoist show how powerful task management systems can also be easy to use and good for both individuals and businesses. Hopefully this app will follow in their footsteps and replace the myriad Microsoft task and project management options that currently exist (Outlook Tasks, Planner, To-Do), like Microsoft is doing consolidating Lync, Skype, and Teams.

author: Rylee's Friend

title: Almost there!
body:
I am a huge fan of Wunderlist, an app that keeps my family and my work organized. So when Microsoft purchased the company, I was skeptical to any new iteration of the to do app. This new Microsoft To-Do app is good, and its close to being a Wunderlist equal. I'm sure the team is already working on these additions but since they are asking for feedback it felt right to give it.

1 - List sharing. My family and I stay organized with shared lists such as the grocery store or home improvement. Would love to see the addition of collaborators on this app.

2 - App integration. Would love to see this integrated with O365 and Outlook.

3 - Subtasks. Projects are kept together with baby steps. Please add subtasks.

4 - Today list. The new My Day list is interesting. I really like that I can choose from suggestions. But if it could also have the automatic addition of tasks I've listed for that day added, it would be perfect. Right now I need to go through the unnecessary step of always adding to My Day.

5 - Multiple accounts. This is a suggestion, but some people like to have work and home separated. I know when I get home, I don't want to think about work. Having an easy way to switch between accounts would be nice rather than signing out and signing in each time.

UPDATE: After posting the initial review a months ago I have yet to see the most important need, List Sharing, integrates into the app. To even start using this app, I must be able to share lists with team members or family. I have also not received any response from MS or Wunderlist regarding this. Hello? Dropping the rating to 1 from 3.

UPDATE #2: The app is still not in my daily workflow and won’t be until it has the features of Wunderlist. It needs folders, and most important, list sharing!! When will this be a feature?

title: A Pinch From the Finish Line
body:
(There is now iPad support!)

I have loved Wunderlist, and Microsoft aims to replace it. The features in To Do are remarkably similar and familiar to Wunderlist users with simplicity and minimalism at its core. With a slimmed-down UI, there's less to distract you and with the flawlessly smooth and responsive controls, you feel like you have a firm grasp on your system. Everything is intuitive and inviting. In addition, I'm from Seattle, so I appreciate the themes.

Right now the only things missing for my own workflow is the ability to have folders and sublists. This is my last reservation for using this app and once this is complete (both are planned), I can officially utilize this as a Wunderlist replacement.

Once I use this in my workflow, I will be most excited about the "My Day" feature. I can use that in tandem with my office' implementation of Kanban to help me see what I committed to getting done today.

I can see this being useful for O365 organizations as well, since it can replace the Outlook tasks, pull assigned tasks from Planner, have inputs with Teams (i.e. Right click a message and select "Create Task")

I'm excited to see where this goes as I wait patiently for the product to bake. Until then, three stars is about where it's at as of now--little more than a college student's obligatory first app.

Long ways to go, but it's an interesting beginning.

title: Fails to live up to potential
body:
I really want to like this app but it’s not near what it should be. 

What I don’t like:
-It lacks folders, sub tasks, task sharing, automation and integration
-Synchronization has been an issue in the past
-Smart lists are replaced by My Day, where you have to manually pick tasks to populate
-There’s no color coding or star system to highlight important tasks. The nearest replacement is using My Day

What I do like:
-It works with Outlook tasks, which is a step in the right direction. 
-The suggestions for My Day could very easily replace smart lists if you could check them off straight from the suggestion window. (Right now you must still add them to My Day)
-The UI is quite nice, despite some bugs still.
-Due dates and Recurring tasks work well

What I’d like to see:
-Tighter integration with Outlook Tasks (assignments, progress, follow ups, color categories)
-Automation (MS flow, email-to-task, Cortana)
-List Folders
-Subtasks (or even just a link to OneNote checklist)

I really wish Microsoft would invest in this team because this could be the definitive productivity app

title: Frustratingly bad
body:
With Microsoft sunsetting Wunderlist, you would think that they'd at least have a suitable replacement. Unfortunately To-Do isn't it. 

Syncing between mobile and desktop works only sometimes, and there's no reliable way to force either app to sync. So you're stuck looking at two wrong versions of the same list until each client bothers to talk to the server.

On top of that, even a single client can have trouble syncing. Sometimes I end up with 2-4 copies of a task that I added only once. 

And let's not even get started on feature parity or UX: still miles behind Wunderlist. Why acquire the company if you're not going to incorporate its IP into your products?

The reason I call To-Do "frustratingly bad" is because I -know- they can do better. If they just re-skinned Wunderlist, they'd have a significantly better product without all of the development effort they're apparently spending on To-Do.

title: Why?  The experience with Outlook (for iOS) was so much better
body:
Thoughts for the product team:

1. Really wished you just rebranded app like you did with Outlook - having two options for tasks breaks the cardinal rule of task management - put them in one place.  I'm sure you have plenty of technical reasons why you're rewriting - but from a user experience standpoint it just feels like you're taking away something we love.  I never felt this way with Outlook (for iOS).
2. The icon / name is a ripoff of the Appigo app - why do this?  
3. Please stick with an icon that looks like an Office 365 icon (like Outlook / OneNote / Teams).  I want to have my row of key office 365 productivity apps - Outlook. OneNote. Teams.  Todo.   
4.  Even better - why not just incorporate this into Outlook?  I'm not sure why I need a different app for tasks.  It's not that way in the desktop version. 

I remember reading an article where Satya Nadella mentioned that Wunderlist was one of his favorite apps - I'm surprised to see this handled the way it has.

I really want this to work - I hope this helps.  I'll update my rating if the ship turns around.

title: Good App, Has Lots of Room for Improvement
body:
I know this app was made to help transition the shutting down of Wunderlist, so eventually To Do will have most, if not all the features Wunderlist has. 

However there are some basic features that should be worked on immediately:

1) App badge support. I would think would be a basic requirement of a to-do app. Even the standard iOS reminders app has app badge support to show how many due items there are that day. 

2) iPad support. There is iPhone support and even Windows 10 app support, which is great. However, there needs to be iPad support as any good to-do app should be multi platform to maximize efficiency.

3) List sharing. This is one of the great features of Wunderlist and allows for collaboration between people. A simple example being sharing a grocery list with my wife. This greatly enhances user experience with the app, and I would love to see this being added.

There are many improvements this app needs, and I understand it's a process so it has a good start. However, it at least needs these 3 updates very soon, or I can foresee many people leaving this app or failing to join because of it.

I personally only have a couple lists I use, and My Day isn't one of them. So every time I open the app, I have to go into the menu and re-open the last list I was using. This alone would turn me off from using the app, but I'm giving it a chance.

It would also be nice to be able to do basic text formatting in the notes (bold, italic, underline, possibly bulleted lists or strikethrough).

I'll keep using it for now. Hopefully the app updates will be coming regularly.

Wunderlist was always a little clunky in my opinion, and setting a recurring task is still clunky. But otherwise, I think MS trimmed it down and made it lean, clean, and sleek.

I'm still wary that MS will screw this up because... Microsoft!, but I like it so far 👊🏻

body:

Third, when I would try to change the due date of a task not created in this app, the app was sometimes unable to do so.  Fourth, there is no widget for the lock screen.  Finally, there is no iPad version.  

With that said, the user interface seems well-designed, and the "My Day" view seems to have potential.  The fact that it reflects what is in Office 365 is critical for organizations that utilize that service.  And finally, it beats the native iOS Reminders app, although that's a pretty low bar.  It will stay installed on my phone with the expectation of major feature updates over the coming weeks.

title: My Day is what I've been looking for
body:
I so far am enjoying the simple My Day feature because what I need the most out of a simple to do list is the ability to quickly prioritize the next tasks in my day. Some of these tasks may become irrelevant tomorrow and I may wind up removing them entirely. That is why having a daily list that resets is actually more valuable for me than being able to customize my tasks to great levels of detail. I appreciate being able to easily add the previous day's tasks to the My Day list on a case-by-case basis. 

I understand that many other reviews focus on this app's limited feature set in comparison to Wunderlist. Indeed, if you have those kind of needs it probably falls short. However if this app continues to be treated as a completely separate solution, I think it serves a different use case very well. Specifically one that most complicated todo apps fail to address in an elegant way.

Otherwise, to see what's due for a day you have to go list by list. It doesn't make much sense. Additionally, it would be really nice to have a default inbox or unassigned tasks list where you can quick-add tasks without having to worry right that moment what their due date will be, or what list they need to go in, etc. Finally, there's no ability to type a due date in manually; you must choose a date from a calendar, which can get annoying of the due date is very far off. On the bright side, the integration with Outlook's task list is great! I was really missing not having that feature on the Outlook mobile app. Hopefully as this app becomes more robust it may even be able to fully integrate into Outlook and replace tasks altogether.

title: Classic clunky Microsoft
body:
This has the clunky Microsoft feel to it alright - a third of the screen is taken up by an unnecessary colored header, which is just a classic waste of space that Microsoft loves. There's of course no way to get rid of it, either. 

You need a Microsoft account which is disappointing, and I can't even use my office 365 account through my university. 

There's no way to make folders like in Wunderlist or Todoist - I assume this will come later, but not sure why it isn't integrated now - seems relatively easy to do. 

When you swipe to get the sidebar to see your lists, it takes up 4/5 of the screen but it's mostly white space - so you have to slide your finger across the entirety of your screen unnecessarily.

Doesn't identify due dates with smart text in the header.

No smart lists so you can only view very limited aspects of your to-do lists. 

The most frustrating "feature" though is the "My Day" list. It's supposed to be a list where you can add anything from your to-do lists to accomplish today specifically. But things that you have scheduled in your lists to be due *today* do not show up in the My Day list unless you specifically add them to it. Why?! Obviously I want to do it *today* if it's scheduled for today. And you can't even see a list of things you have due today unless you add them one by one to the My Day list. It makes zero sense which is why I guess Microsoft was so keen on implementing it.

I can already tell Microsoft is going to botch this like they do all the other apps they buy, steal, and turn into a clunky Microsoft Outlook-integrated wasted-space lacking-basic-features kind of app. Thanks for nothing.

title: Ứng dụng tốt để thay thế reminder của iphone và Macbook
body:
Kể từ khi nâng cấp lên iOS 13 toàn bộ lịch nhắc nhở của tôi trên iPhone, iPad và Macbook gặp sự cố làm đảo lộn cuộc sống của tôi. Tôi đã cố gắng khắc phục nhưng không được, Reninder gần như tê liệt khi bị nâng cấp, các lỗi xuất hiện thường xuyên, các thiết bị cũ không thể hoạt động reminder do cơ sở dữ liệu reminder đã bị nâng cấp. Thật là tệ hại.
Tôi đã quyết định chọn một phần mềm khác tốt hơn để quản lý công việc, và tôi thấy Microsoft To Do là phần mềm tuyệt vời. Có thể đồng bộ trên mọi thiết bị, từ laptop cho đến tablet, mobile, ... mà không bị bó hẹp trong hệ sinh thái của Apple.
Tôi nghĩ rằng đã đến lúc tôi hủy tất cả các phần mềm reminder trên các thiết bị của Apple để chuyển sang dùng Microsoft To Do vì tôi cần sự thuận tiện, chuẩn chỉ, và thật ổn định, đặc biệt là danh sách những công việc của tôi.

title: Great app, but sluggish
body: I always loved using this app to stay productive, and the syncing across multiple devices and ecosystems makes it pretty convenient. The app has recently become very sluggish, and the sync appears to be slowing things down. Scrolling in lists with many reminders seems to cause the app to experience some jitter - looks like a lazy-load of items on a list. It would be great to have the app more snappy and responsive, especially when adding items to your list on the go. I often use the app to set reminders, and it would be great if you could add reminders from within the iOS widget, as opposed to opening the entire app, waiting a bit, and then creating the reminder. Love the app, but it needs some optimisations to make it more responsive… sync tasks can happen silently in the background and should not affect foreground usage.

Honestly I’m so impressed. This rarely happens, but after using this app today, I actually thought to myself “This is such an incredibly useful tool for my life, I wonder what add-on’s I could purchase...” 

So I went to my AppStore and checked and there’s literally no in-app purchases. 

It then all made sense. This is such powerful branding for Microsoft. Honestly, great job guys! Now everytime I consider using y’all, I’ll remember and associate this quality product you guys produced completely free to the market. I salute that. Thank you
